Step 1 — Inventory the real product. Read the repo to find what actually exists and works. Look at: app/(marketing)/ (existing marketing pages + what products are advertised), lib/actions*.ts, worker/ (provisioning, hosting, migration, ssl), the ROADMAP/docs, prisma/schema.prisma. - Differentiators that are REAL: one-command / AI-assisted deploy ("Build with AI"), the "Matrix" multi-app build feature (lib + /matrix), FREE website migration (the migration engine in worker/migrate*), automatic SSL, one-click apps/WordPress, per-account isolation, DDoS protection, dedicated IPs, "Claude Code pre-installed" on servers, free tools suite (/tools).
- The genuinely distinctive angle vs Hostinger/Vercel/DigitalOcean: the AI-assisted "describe it and it deploys" + Matrix + free migration.

Step 2 — Propose ONE unifying concept. Given those real features and the audience (builders/indie hackers/SMBs), propose a SINGLE, focused, ownable creative concept/metaphor for the homepage — one big idea that ties the products together and can carry an interactive hero + scroll-driven sections. Give it a name and a one-line thesis. Then map each real Nxeon feature to a section/scene within that concept. Include how a "Matrix" visualization and a "migration" animation fit naturally into the concept (not bolted on).

Step 3 — Give the section-by-section outline for the homepage under that ONE concept: hero, the scroll scenes, social proof, pricing/CTA — with the real feature each showcases and the intended emotional beat.

Be concrete and grounded in the actual codebase. Return: (a) the verified real-feature inventory, (b) the single concept with thesis, (c) the section-by-section outline.

## (b) The single unifying concept

### Concept: **"The Command Deck"** — *Say it. It ships.*

**One-line thesis:** *Every other host hands you an empty box and a login. Nxeon hands you a command deck — you tell it what you want in plain English, watch it materialize on infrastructure you own, and it can even go fetch your old server and bring it here.*

**Why this is the one idea, and why it's ownable:** The literal, code-true throughline of Nxeon is **the console**. Claude CLI ships on every box; "Build with AI" is a plan-you-approve console; the flagship is literally called **Matrix** — a *grid of live build consoles*; the migration wizard narrates a live console; even the free tools are console-flavored. Competitors can't run this metaphor because they don't put an AI terminal on the machine. The Command Deck turns Nxeon's actual UI primitive into the site's spine — nothing is bolted on because the whole product already *is* this.

**The visual system:** one continuous dark canvas — "the deck" — with a persistent, glowing command line at its heart and a **living grid** behind it (the same visual language as the Matrix product). You don't scroll past disconnected sections; you scroll *down the deck*, and each scene is a new intent typed into the line that summons the matching product onto the grid — then dissolves to the next. Blue→purple gradient, glassmorphism, monospace accents. Premium-honest, not fairy-dust: every "summon" resolves into a **real** artifact (a real port, a real plan-to-approve, a real "and here's what we flagged" list), which is exactly the brand's no-overclaiming voice from `/migrate`.

| Real feature | Scene on the deck | Why it fits the metaphor |
|---|---|---|

| VPS + one-click images | Prompt "spin up a server," a node lights up on the grid, image chips (OS/panel/app) snap on | A summon that resolves to a real box with full root |
| **Matrix** | The single console **splits into six live build cells** on the grid; mirror-mode fans one prompt across 3 servers | The grid literally *is* Matrix — the site's visual language and the flagship product are the same object |
| **Free migration** | A **foreign, off-brand server** drifts in from the left edge; its blocks (files/DBs/Docker) fly across the deck and snap into a Nxeon node; a short "flagged for you" ticket prints | Migration = "bring another deck's cargo onto ours" — motion is inherent, not decorative |
| Game servers | Prompt "run a Minecraft server," a game cell boots with a live player count | Same summon gesture, different cargo |
| Web hosting / WordPress / auto-SSL | "Host my WordPress site," a site cell lights, a padlock (SSL) clicks shut automatically | The deck handles the boring parts silently |
| Domains + email | "Point my domain here," a globe node wires to the grid; a mail node attaches | Networking the deck to the outside world |
| Block storage | "Add more disk," a volume slab docks onto a running node without rebooting it | Grow the deck without tearing it down |
| Free tools | A "utility drawer" on the deck — WHOIS/DNS/SSL checkers as instant, no-login deck instruments | Tools that live on the command deck itself |
| Dedicated IP / DDoS / monitoring | Ambient: a shield ring + a steady "24/7 monitoring" pulse around the whole grid | The deck's always-on defensive layer |

**Persistent element:** the command line and grid canvas carry through the whole page; sections are *scenes on one deck*, not separated cards.

**1. Hero — "Say it. It ships."** *(interactive)*
- **Feature:** Build-with-AI + Claude CLI on every box.
- **What it does:** Live command line auto-cycles real intents ("build a SaaS with Stripe," "migrate my old server," "run a Rust server").
